steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Rivetbay on this bench turns event descriptions into field decoders. Descriptions live at `/app/rivetbay/evd/*.evd`. One mill pass must refresh `/app/rivetbay/intake/current.ledger` from those files and write one `/app/rivetbay/emitters/<name>.kdec` per description discovered on that run. `/app/bin/rivetbay mill` is that pass; `/app/bin/rivetbay decode <frame>` prints JSON for a sample under `/app/rivetbay/frames`. A description with no decoder decodes as unknown.

Some descriptions on disk currently finish mill without a matching `.kdec`, decode as unknown, and leave emitters short of the on-disk descriptions; mill must exit non-zero when decoders are fewer than descriptions. One mill subprocess must leave emitters equal to the descriptions present for that run, and decode of a newly added event must print its fields.

Update the C code in the mill pipeline under `/app/rivetbay` so each pass regenerates the ledger and `.kdec` files from descriptions on disk, then rebuild `/app/bin/rivetbay`. Hand-written ledger or decoder files are not enough. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/rivetbay mill` and `/app/bin/rivetbay decode` on fresh descriptions and frames. Ledger lines are `name|relpath|field:kind,...` with kinds `u8` and `u16` in description order; mill must keep prior ledger row order and append newly discovered descriptions after existing rows. Each `.kdec` begins with the `KDEC1` header line, then `NAME <name>`, then one `field kind` line per description field in that same order. Decode output is one JSON object with string `kind` and `name` keys and an integer `fields` map keyed by description field names when a decoder exists. Frame bytes are a 4-byte big-endian name length, the name, then packed big-endian field payloads.

Plan: Inspect the project tree and relevant source/build files, then examine sample descriptions, ledger, emitters, and the rivetbay launcher/binary metadata. This will establish the input format and locate the mill pipeline code before making changes.

steps.message:
Analysis: There are eight descriptions but only seven ledger rows and emitters; galley_hatch is omitted. The visible driver primes a sheet, discovers descriptions, writes the ledger, emits decoders, and returns count_gap(), so the defect is likely in shared sheet/discovery state or emission iteration. We need inspect complete implementations, including /app/millscore tally support, before patching.
Plan: Print the discovery, snapshot/sheet, emitter, warmup, and tally implementations without output truncation. Also inspect operational notes and run the current mill once to capture its exit status and resulting counts. Then patch the pipeline based on the actual state-flow defect.

arguments.keystrokes: cd /app/rivetbay; for f in forgekit/discover.c forgekit/snapshot.c forgekit/emit.c forgekit/warmup.c forgekit/sheet.h; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat "$f"; done
echo '===== millscore ====='; find /app/millscore -maxdepth 2 -type f -print; for f in /app/millscore/*.[ch]; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat "$f"; done
cd /app/rivetbay; for f in notes/*.txt; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat "$f"; done; echo '===== Makefile bytes ====='; sed -n l Makefile

/app/bin/rivetbay mill; rc=$?; echo "mill_rc=$rc"; echo "evd=$(find /app/rivetbay/evd -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.evd' | wc -l) ledger=$(grep -cve '^[[:space:]]*$' /app/rivetbay/intake/current.ledger) emitters=$(find /app/rivetbay/emitters -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.kdec' | wc -l)"; cat /app/rivetbay/intake/current.ledger

steps.message:
Analysis: The defect is confirmed: snapshot.c primes both the sheet and emission cap from stale intake/mill_open, and never loads the newly regenerated current.ledger. Thus discovery writes eight rows, but emission remains capped at seven stale rows. emit.c also reverses field order, and emitters from removed descriptions are never deleted. count_gap compares stale in-memory sheet rows to emitter count, explaining the false zero exit. Discovery additionally reconstructs prior paths as <name>.evd rather than preserving/matching actual discovered files.
Plan: Rewrite discovery to scan current .evd files, preserve the order of still-present prior ledger names, refresh every row from disk, and append newly discovered records. Change snapshot pouring to load the newly written ledger and derive its current row count. Change emission to remove old .kdec files first, emit every ledger row, and preserve field order. Add a final driver check comparing on-disk .evd and .kdec counts so fewer decoders always yields non-zero, then rebuild and test both existing and newly added descriptions.

arguments.keystrokes: /app/bin/rivetbay mill; rc=$?; echo "mill_rc=$rc"; echo "evd=$(find evd -maxdepth 1 -name '*.evd' -type f | wc -l) ledger=$(grep -cve '^[[:space:]]*$' intake/current.ledger) emitters=$(find emitters -maxdepth 1 -name '*.kdec' -type f | wc -l)"; cat intake/current.ledger; echo '--- galley decoder'; cat emitters/galley_hatch.kdec; echo '--- galley decode'; /app/bin/rivetbay decode frames/galley_hatch.bin

cat > evd/verifier_filename.evd <<'EOF'
NAME fresh_event
FIELD first u8
FIELD second u16
FIELD third u8
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
import struct
name=b'fresh_event'
open('frames/fresh_event.bin','wb').write(struct.pack('>I',len(name))+name+struct.pack('>BHB',7,513,9))
PY
/app/bin/rivetbay mill; rc=$?; echo "fresh_mill_rc=$rc"; tail -n 2 intake/current.ledger; echo '--- fresh kdec'; cat emitters/fresh_event.kdec; echo '--- fresh decode'; /app/bin/rivetbay decode frames/fresh_event.bin

steps.message:
Analysis: The rebuilt pipeline now produces all eight required emitters, preserves description field order, decodes galley_hatch correctly, and successfully discovers a fresh event whose filename differs from its NAME. The fresh event was appended after prior ledger rows and decoded all u8/u16 values correctly. Temporary verification files remain and must be removed so the bench returns to its intended dataset. We should also verify that a subsequent mill removes stale emitters and restores exactly eight outputs.
Plan: Remove the temporary fresh description and frame, deliberately leave its generated decoder as a stale file, then run mill to confirm stale cleanup, correct counts, stable prior ledger order, and successful decode. Finally rebuild once more and report the resulting binary and mill status.

arguments.keystrokes: cd /app/rivetbay && rm -f evd/verifier_filename.evd frames/fresh_event.bin && test -f emitters/fresh_event.kdec && echo 'stale emitter present before mill'; /app/bin/rivetbay mill; rc=$?; echo "cleanup_mill_rc=$rc"; echo "evd=$(find evd -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.evd' | wc -l) ledger=$(grep -cve '^[[:space:]]*$' intake/current.ledger) emitters=$(find emitters -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.kdec' | wc -l)"; test ! -e emitters/fresh_event.kdec && echo 'stale emitter removed'; cat intake/current.ledger

set -e; cd /app/rivetbay; test "$(find evd -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.evd' | wc -l)" -eq "$(find emitters -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.kdec' | wc -l)"; test "$(grep -cve '^[[:space:]]*$' intake/current.ledger)" -eq "$(find evd -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.evd' | wc -l)"; /app/bin/rivetbay decode frames/galley_hatch.bin; make hull >/dev/null; /app/bin/rivetbay mill; echo "final_mill_rc=$?"; file /app/bin/rivetbay
